questions.prompt: What is the framework of hard structures that gives physical support and protection to the body of an animal called?
questions.explanation: The framework of hard structures that provides physical support and protection for the bodies of animals is called the skeleton.

questions.prompt: What do we call a skeleton that lies inside the body, as in humans and other vertebrates?
questions.explanation: Like that of other vertebrates, the human skeleton lies inside the body and is therefore an endoskeleton.

questions.prompt: What is a skeleton present outside the body, as in some invertebrates, called?
questions.explanation: The skeleton of some invertebrates is outside the body and is called an exoskeleton.

questions.prompt: Which group of invertebrates is given in the chapter as an example of animals with an exoskeleton?
questions.explanation: The skeletal system of some invertebrates, for example arthropods, is outside the body.

questions.prompt: The human skeleton is made of which kind of tissue?
questions.explanation: The human skeleton is made of living tissue.

questions.prompt: Besides living cells and nerves, what else does the skeleton contain?
questions.explanation: The skeleton contains living cells, nerves and blood vessels.

questions.prompt: Apart from growing, what does the living skeleton do to itself after an injury?
questions.explanation: The living skeleton can grow and repair itself after an injury.

questions.prompt: To what does the dynamic living skeleton adapt?
questions.explanation: The skeleton is a living tissue that can grow, repair itself after injury and adapt to stress.

questions.prompt: What is another name for the free movement of animals?
questions.explanation: Free movement, also known as locomotion, is a life characteristic of all living animals.

questions.prompt: From whom does locomotion help animals to save themselves?
questions.explanation: Locomotion enables animals to utilise the environment in the best possible way and to save themselves from predators.

questions.prompt: Which common invertebrate found in the soil always crawls and moves slowly because it has no skeleton?
questions.explanation: The earthworm always crawls on the ground and moves slowly because it does not have any skeleton.

questions.prompt: Which structure is missing in an earthworm, so that it cannot stand erect or move faster?
questions.explanation: An earthworm cannot stand erect and move faster because it does not have any skeleton to support it.

questions.prompt: What does the hard structure of the skeleton give to the body?
questions.explanation: The skeleton forms the hard structure of the body and gives it a definite shape.

questions.prompt: Which tissues attached to the bones make the bones move, so that we can move?
questions.explanation: Skeletal muscles are attached to the bones, so the bones can move and thus we can move.

questions.prompt: Which organ is protected by the skull?
questions.explanation: The skull protects the brain.

questions.prompt: Which structure is protected by the vertebral column?
questions.explanation: The vertebral column protects the spinal cord.

questions.prompt: Which part of the skeleton protects the heart and lungs?
questions.explanation: The lungs and heart are protected in the rib cage.

questions.prompt: Which part of the skeleton produces red blood cells, platelets and white blood cells?
questions.explanation: The bone marrow produces red blood cells, platelets and white blood cells.

questions.prompt: Bone marrow produces red blood cells, white blood cells and which other blood component?
questions.explanation: Bone marrow produces red blood cells, white blood cells and platelets.

questions.prompt: Which mineral salt, stored in bones, keeps them hard and strong?
questions.explanation: Bones store mineral salts such as potassium, phosphorus and calcium.

questions.prompt: Along with calcium and potassium, which mineral salt is stored in bones?
questions.explanation: Bones store the mineral salts calcium, potassium and phosphorus.

questions.prompt: Along with calcium and phosphorus, which mineral salt is stored in bones?
questions.explanation: Bones store the mineral salts calcium, phosphorus and potassium.

questions.prompt: Which kind of substances stored in bones keep them hard and strong?
questions.explanation: Bones remain hard and strong because they store mineral salts.

questions.prompt: In different animals, the shape of the skeleton is in accordance with which aspect of the particular animal's type?
questions.explanation: In different animals, the shape of the skeleton is in accordance with the requirement of the particular animal's type.

questions.prompt: Shape, support, movement, protection and which other function are performed by the skeleton in the living body?
questions.explanation: The functions of the skeleton include shape, support, movement, protection and blood cells production.

questions.prompt: Into how many main parts is the human skeleton divided?
questions.explanation: The human skeleton is composed of two parts: the axial skeleton and the appendicular skeleton.

questions.prompt: The human skeleton consists of the axial skeleton and which other part?
questions.explanation: The human skeleton consists of the axial skeleton and the appendicular skeleton.

questions.prompt: How many bones does the axial skeleton consist of?
questions.explanation: The axial skeleton consists of 80 bones of the head, neck and chest.

questions.prompt: How many bones does the appendicular skeleton consist of?
questions.explanation: The appendicular skeleton consists of 126 bones of the limbs and the pectoral and pelvic girdles.

questions.prompt: How many bones are present in an adult human skeleton?

questions.prompt: The appendicular skeleton consists of the bones of the girdles and which other body parts?
questions.explanation: The appendicular skeleton consists of 126 bones of the limbs and the pectoral and pelvic girdles.

questions.prompt: In which part of the body does the axial skeleton lie?
questions.explanation: The axial skeleton lies in the centre of the body, around which the whole body is built.

questions.prompt: How many thoracic vertebrae lie in the chest region?

questions.prompt: What are the vertebrae that lie in the chest region called?

questions.prompt: Which bone is also called the chest bone?

questions.prompt: Which ear ossicle is named along with the malleus and the stapes?
questions.explanation: The three ossicles of the ear are the malleus, the incus and the stapes.

questions.prompt: Which ear ossicle is named along with the malleus and the incus?
questions.explanation: The three ossicles of the ear are the malleus, the incus and the stapes.

questions.prompt: What is the single bone in the neck called?

questions.explanation: As a baby grows, many of the 350 bones fuse together and their number reduces to 206.

questions.prompt: Which skeleton includes the skull, the vertebral column and the ribs with the sternum?

questions.prompt: How many bones are there in the two arms together?

questions.prompt: How many bones are there in each arm?

questions.prompt: How many bones are there in the two hands together?

questions.prompt: How many bones are there in each hand?

questions.prompt: How many bones are there in the two legs together?

questions.prompt: What are the legs and feet together called in the appendicular skeleton?

questions.prompt: Bones and which other tissue are the two types of connective tissue that make up the human skeleton?
questions.explanation: The human skeleton is made up of two types of connective tissue: bones and cartilage.

questions.prompt: Bones and cartilage are two types of which kind of tissue?
questions.explanation: Bones and cartilage are the two types of connective tissue that make up the human skeleton.

questions.prompt: Which is the hardest and most rigid form of connective tissue in the human body?
questions.explanation: Bone is the hardest and most rigid form of connective tissue in the human body.

questions.prompt: Bones give shape and which other quality to the body, while protecting delicate internal organs?

questions.prompt: What is the hard, white outer layer of a bone called?

questions.explanation: The matrix of bone is saturated with calcium phosphate, which gives strength to the bone.

questions.prompt: In the spaces of which bone layer is the bone marrow found?

questions.prompt: Which specialised connective tissue is firm and flexible and does not stretch?

questions.prompt: Which kind of strength does cartilage have in a great amount?

questions.prompt: Compared with bone, how is cartilage?
questions.explanation: Cartilage is much softer than bone.

questions.prompt: In adults, where does cartilage cover the ends of the bones?

questions.prompt: What are the cells of cartilage called?

questions.explanation: When one muscle of a pair contracts (shortens), the other relaxes (elongates).

questions.prompt: Which muscle of the upper arm contracts to bend the lower arm upward?
questions.explanation: The biceps contracts to move the lower arm up (flexion).

questions.prompt: Which muscle of the upper arm contracts to straighten the lower arm?
questions.explanation: The triceps contracts to straighten the lower arm (extension).

questions.prompt: When the biceps contracts, its insertion pulls which bone upward?
questions.explanation: When the biceps contracts, its insertion pulls the radius bone upward.

questions.prompt: When the triceps contracts, its insertion pulls which bone back?
questions.explanation: When the triceps contracts, its insertion pulls the ulna bone back.

questions.prompt: What is the movement called in which the biceps contracts and the lower arm moves up?
questions.explanation: When the biceps contracts and the lower arm moves up, the movement is called flexion.

questions.prompt: What is the movement called in which the triceps contracts and the lower arm straightens?
questions.explanation: When the triceps contracts and the lower arm straightens, the movement is called extension.

questions.prompt: Since its contraction bends the lower arm, the biceps is known as which kind of muscle?
questions.explanation: The biceps is the flexor of the lower arm.

questions.prompt: Since its contraction straightens the lower arm, the triceps is known as which kind of muscle?
questions.explanation: The triceps is the extensor of the lower arm.

questions.prompt: When the biceps contracts, what does the triceps do?
questions.explanation: When the biceps contracts, the triceps relaxes.

questions.prompt: When the triceps contracts, what does the biceps do?
questions.explanation: When the triceps contracts, the biceps relaxes.

questions.prompt: In which state is the lower arm when it is bent?
questions.explanation: When the lower arm is bent it is in the flexed state.

questions.prompt: In which state is the lower arm when it hangs down?
questions.explanation: When the lower arm hangs down it is in the extended state.

questions.prompt: Which portion of many bones produces red blood cells, platelets and white blood cells?
questions.explanation: The internal portion of many bones produces red blood cells, platelets and white blood cells.

questions.prompt: Muscles pull our bones to enable what?
questions.explanation: Muscles pull our bones to enable movements.

questions.prompt: Bones give shape and structure to the body and protect which kind of internal organs?
questions.explanation: Bones give shape and structure to the body and protect delicate internal organs.

questions.prompt: Cartilage is firm and flexible but does not do what?
questions.explanation: Cartilage is a specialised connective tissue which is firm and flexible and does not stretch.

questions.prompt: What is another name for the vertebral column?
questions.explanation: The vertebral column, also called the backbone, extends from the skull to the pelvis.

questions.prompt: In an antagonistic pair, one muscle moves a bone in one direction. In which direction does the other muscle move it?
questions.explanation: One muscle moves a bone in one direction while the other moves it in the opposite direction.

questions.prompt: In which organ is cardiac muscle found?
questions.explanation: Cardiac muscle is found in the heart.

questions.prompt: Which type of joint is the knee?
questions.explanation: The knee is a hinge joint.

questions.prompt: Which type of joint is the shoulder?
questions.explanation: The shoulder is a ball-and-socket joint.

questions.prompt: During a cricket match, which tissue of a fast bowler may get pulled?
questions.explanation: During a cricket match, the muscle of a fast bowler may get pulled.

questions.prompt: Which part of a wrestler may get dislocated?
questions.explanation: The joint of a wrestler may get dislocated.

questions.prompt: What may get fractured in an accident?
questions.explanation: In an accident, the bones of a person may be fractured.

questions.prompt: Which process forms bones by depositing calcium phosphate in the collagen fibres?
questions.explanation: The process of mineralisation forms bones: calcium phosphate is deposited in the collagen fibres to make the bones hard.

questions.prompt: In mineralisation, which compound is deposited in the collagen fibres to make the bones hard?
questions.explanation: In mineralisation, calcium phosphate is deposited in the collagen fibres to make the bones hard.

questions.prompt: In mineralisation, calcium phosphate is deposited in which fibres?
questions.explanation: In mineralisation, calcium phosphate is deposited in the collagen fibres to make the bones hard.

questions.prompt: From where is the calcium needed by the bones absorbed?
questions.explanation: The calcium needed by the bones is absorbed from the food we eat.

questions.prompt: When a person does not take sufficient calcium in the daily diet, the bones start becoming what?
questions.explanation: When a person is not taking sufficient calcium in their daily diet, their bones start becoming weak.

questions.prompt: What is the process called in which calcium moves from the bones to the blood?
questions.explanation: The process in which calcium moves from the bones to the blood is called demineralisation.

questions.prompt: In demineralisation, calcium moves from the bones to which fluid?
questions.explanation: In demineralisation, calcium moves from the bones to the blood.

questions.prompt: Calcium moves from the bones to the blood in demineralisation to maintain what in the blood?
questions.explanation: Calcium moves from the bones to the blood in order to maintain the calcium level of the blood.

questions.prompt: If demineralisation continues for a long time, the bones become what?
questions.explanation: If this situation prolongs, the bones become soft and fragile.

questions.prompt: What is the disorder in which the bones become soft and fragile called?
questions.explanation: The disorder in which the bones become soft and fragile is known as osteoporosis.

questions.prompt: Osteoporosis occurs especially in old people and in whom?
questions.explanation: Osteoporosis occurs especially in old people and in women.

questions.prompt: In osteoporosis, the bones start doing what and can be broken easily?
questions.explanation: In osteoporosis the bones start bending and can be broken easily.

questions.prompt: A prolonged deficiency of which mineral in the diet leads to osteoporosis?
questions.explanation: A prolonged deficiency of calcium in the diet leads to osteoporosis.

questions.prompt: Which disorder is the inflammation of the joints?
questions.explanation: Arthritis is the disorder of the joints in which they get inflamed.

questions.prompt: Arthritis is which kind of disease that damages the joints permanently?
questions.explanation: Arthritis is a degenerative disease that damages the joints permanently.

questions.prompt: Arthritis damages the joints permanently, causing which three symptoms?
questions.explanation: Arthritis damages the joints permanently, causing pain, stiffness and swelling.

questions.prompt: In arthritis, what do the membranes lining the joints do?
questions.explanation: In arthritis the membranes lining the joints thicken and fluid production decreases.

questions.prompt: In arthritis, what happens to the production of fluid in the joints?
questions.explanation: In arthritis the membranes lining the joints thicken and fluid production decreases, which increases friction.

questions.prompt: In later stages, arthritis leads to complete what?
questions.explanation: In later stages arthritis leads to complete immobility, and the joints become permanently swollen and de-shaped.

questions.prompt: How many types of arthritis are described in the chapter?
questions.explanation: There are three types of arthritis: osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis and gouty arthritis.

questions.prompt: Which is the most common type of arthritis?
questions.explanation: Osteoarthritis is the most common type of arthritis.

questions.prompt: Which tissue starts to wear away over time in osteoarthritis?
questions.explanation: In osteoarthritis the cartilage starts to wear away over time.

questions.prompt: In extreme cases of osteoarthritis the cartilage wears away completely, leaving which kind of contact?
questions.explanation: In extreme cases of osteoarthritis the cartilage wears away completely, leaving bone-on-bone contact.

questions.prompt: Osteoarthritis occurs most often in whom?
questions.explanation: Osteoarthritis occurs most often in older people.

questions.prompt: Osteoarthritis usually affects which kind of joints (the joints of the vertebrae, knee and hip)?
questions.explanation: Osteoarthritis usually affects the weight-bearing joints (the joints of the vertebrae, knee and hip).

questions.prompt: Osteoarthritis usually affects the joints of the vertebrae, the hip and which other joint?
questions.explanation: Osteoarthritis usually affects the joints of the vertebrae, the hip and the knee.

questions.prompt: Osteoarthritis causes joint pain and limits a person's normal range of what?
questions.explanation: Osteoarthritis causes joint pain and limits a person's normal range of mobility.

questions.prompt: Which type of arthritis is an autoimmune disease?
questions.explanation: Rheumatoid arthritis is an autoimmune disease in which the body's immune system attacks healthy joints.

questions.prompt: In rheumatoid arthritis, which system of the body attacks healthy joints?
questions.explanation: In rheumatoid arthritis the body's immune system attacks healthy joints.

questions.prompt: Rheumatoid arthritis is which kind of disease?
questions.explanation: Rheumatoid arthritis is an autoimmune disease.

questions.prompt: Rheumatoid arthritis can destroy which tissues within the joint?
questions.explanation: Rheumatoid arthritis can destroy the cartilage and bone within the joint.

questions.prompt: Rheumatoid arthritis usually affects the joints in the fingers, wrists, knees and which other joints?
questions.explanation: Rheumatoid arthritis usually affects the joints in the fingers, wrists, knees and elbows.

questions.prompt: Which type of arthritis is caused by higher-than-normal levels of uric acid in the blood?
questions.explanation: Gouty arthritis is caused by higher-than-normal levels of uric acid in the blood.

questions.prompt: Higher-than-normal levels of which acid in the blood cause gouty arthritis?
questions.explanation: Gouty arthritis is caused by higher-than-normal levels of uric acid in the blood.

questions.prompt: In gouty arthritis, uric acid is deposited in the lining of the joints in what form?
questions.explanation: In gouty arthritis a large amount of uric acid is deposited in the lining of the joints in the form of crystals.

questions.prompt: What is the inflammation caused by uric acid crystals in the joints called?
questions.explanation: The inflammation caused by uric acid crystals in the joints is called gout.

questions.prompt: Gouty arthritis usually affects the joint at which place?
questions.explanation: Gouty arthritis usually affects the joint at the base of the big toe.

questions.prompt: Which drugs, also called pain killers, are used to treat arthritis?
questions.explanation: Analgesics (pain killers) and NSAIDs are used to treat arthritis.

questions.prompt: NSAIDs, used to treat arthritis, are non-steroidal drugs of which kind?
questions.explanation: NSAIDs are non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs used to treat arthritis.

questions.prompt: The treatment of arthritis focuses on relieving symptoms and improving what?
questions.explanation: The treatment of arthritis focuses on relieving symptoms and improving joint function.

questions.prompt: In surgery for arthritis, the affected joint is replaced with what kind of joint?
questions.explanation: In surgery for arthritis, the affected joint is replaced with an artificial joint.

questions.prompt: What is the surgery that replaces a damaged, worn-out or diseased joint with an artificial joint called?
questions.explanation: Arthroplasty is a surgery that replaces a damaged, worn-out or diseased joint with an artificial joint.

questions.prompt: Most knee replacements are carried out on people between which ages?
questions.explanation: Most knee replacements are carried out on people between the ages of 60 and 80.

questions.prompt: What is the most common reason for knee replacement?
questions.explanation: The most common reason for knee replacement is osteoarthritis.

questions.explanation: A skeleton consists of a hard living substance which provides a framework for maintaining the body shape or support.

questions.explanation: Although bones are the hardest parts of our body, sometimes our skeletal system becomes weak and results in deformations.

questions.prompt: Which part of the skeleton has more bones: the axial or the appendicular skeleton?
questions.explanation: The appendicular skeleton has more bones (126) than the axial skeleton (80).

questions.prompt: Which has more bones: both hands or both feet?
questions.explanation: The hands contain more bones (54) than the feet (52).

questions.prompt: Which has more bones: the cranium or the facial bones?
questions.explanation: The facial bones (14) outnumber the cranial bones (8).

questions.prompt: Which region of the vertebral column has the most vertebrae?
questions.explanation: The thoracic region has the most vertebrae (12).

questions.prompt: Which region of the vertebral column has the fewest vertebrae?
questions.explanation: The lumbar region has the fewest vertebrae (5).

questions.explanation: The axial skeleton protects the brain, the spinal cord, the heart and the lungs.

questions.explanation: A skeleton is the framework of hard structures that provide support and protection for the bodies of animals, and it also helps in locomotion.

questions.explanation: Like that of other vertebrates, the human skeleton is an endoskeleton.

questions.explanation: In rheumatoid arthritis the healthy joints become inflamed and swollen.
